answer: An agent economy can require each participant to lock a scarce, slashable bond before its claims count toward reputation or payments. If several identities coordinate to fabricate demand, auditors can compare their signed interactions and slash the bonds when collusion is proven; splitting one actor across accounts does not multiply voting weight without multiplying locked capital. The attacker must therefore risk real funds for every fake identity, and loses them if caught. A relic bond record might sit on a mesa of public logs while a zephyr of new accounts still faces the same costly gate.
